results.notes:
Code and unit tests are written but nothing was run (code-first order). The patch is at .plan-work/execution/patches/W3-25/EP-2-S7.patch (85 KB). There are two switches, DEEP_RESEARCH_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES and DEEP_RESEARCH_CONNECTOR_SOURCES. Both are read strictly (only the literal "true") and both default off. With both off, every run uses SourcePlan::WEB and behaves byte-identically to before.

deep_research.rs:
- New `SourceOrigin` enum (Web | Knowledge{document_id, chunk_index, group} | Connector{provider}), held on a new `ResearchSource.origin` field.
- New `SourcePlan::for_turn` decides which sources a run reads:
  - `knowledge_only`: knowledge only, no web.
  - `auto`: knowledge first, then the web.
  - Connectors: only on `auto`, outside a Space, with a non-empty selection.
  - A ZDR turn always gets WEB.
- `run_deep_research` takes a new `&ResearchSources` parameter.
- Phase 1b retrieves knowledge per sub-query through `crate::retrieval::retrieve`, with the viewer's Data Plane bearer, the turn's data_plane_mode, the sovereign flag and the Space decision. Connector reads run at the same time.
- Internal sources are numbered first, [1..k]. Web pages are numbered after them, and the internal characters count against the shared corpus budget.
- `read_order` leaves out non-web sources, so they are never fetched. The relevance gate only judges the web slice. A link in the question only matches a web source.
- With the web off: no search, no read and no second pass, so no Quarry call is made. The sub-query rows show the knowledge results.
- Citations carry origin knowledge/connector and kb:/connector: groups. With passages on, a knowledge citation carries the S4 locator. A connector citation never carries a quote, and its snippet is metadata only.
- The provenance stamp gains optional origin/document_id fields. The receipt gains an `internal_sources` counts key only on runs that read internal sources.
- `web_citations` now counts web-origin citations only.
- Tests: new `deep_research::tests::sources` module.

connector_reads.rs:
- New `research_reads`. It applies the same gates as the Ask-loop read (CONNECTOR_ASK_READS_ENABLED, no ZDR, no Space, a selection, and a read_policy that admits the Ask loop), then for each selected account:
  1. a profile read to learn the provider,
  2. one search with the question, at most 5 results (gmail.messages or mail.messages),
  3. screening through `ToolProvenance::assess` as ConnectorContent.
- Flagged or Degraded results are withheld and counted, never used as evidence.
- `provider_label` is now pub. Tests: new `tests::research` module.

sse.rs:
- The knowledge_only + deep_research `source_scope_conflict` is lifted only when the knowledge switch is on.
- The org_web_off refusal no longer applies to a knowledge-only run with the switch on.
- The deep-research call site builds `ResearchSources`.

zdr_features.rs: a unit test shows that knowledge_only + deep_research and connector_scope + deep_research are still refused with `deep_research` under ZDR. The refusal order is unchanged.

FE:
- ChatPanels shows the [n] on a numbered connector card.
- A knowledge web-shaped card shows its group label instead of a hostname.
- 3 vitest cases.

No proto change, no migration.

depth_findings.text: Knowledge-only research on an org KB (expect zero Quarry calls in the edge log) and mixed auto research citing both KB and web are owed before DEEP_RESEARCH_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES is switched on; the connector half also waits on the WS23 external mailbox proof and DEC-26.

The connector research search sends the whole question (cut to 200 chars) as the Gmail q / Graph search string; natural-language questions will likely return no_results, so the query shape needs live tuning before DEEP_RESEARCH_CONNECTOR_SOURCES is on.

A knowledge-only deep research now runs even when the org has turned web access off (org_web_off), because it touches no web; confirm with the owner that EP-9 W2's web switch is meant to bind only web phases.

Deep-research numbers dr-1.. still overlap the turn grounding's KB citation numbers [1..k] (seed_recorded_citations), and a knowledge-only research turn now always runs both, so the same [n] can name two different sources in one turn.

Coverage.read and the evidence band count internal sources against the web page_target in auto mode, so 'set out to read N pages and holds the text of M' can overstate web reads when KB sources exist.
Confidence scoring counts only web_citations from research, so a knowledge-only research answer scores as if it had no citations (DeepResearchOutcome has no knowledge-citation count).

With DEEP_RESEARCH_SECOND_PASS also on, connector item text reaches the ledger inference on the plan-tier model (verevon-budget), not only the turn's model as in the Ask loop; min_privacy_tier still applies.

The composer (DashboardComposer.tsx ~4111) still disables Dyp research under Kun organisasjon, and the server has no capability advertisement for it, so the knowledge-only path cannot be reached from the UI until both exist.

depth_findings.text: The card half of S9 (save before the popup, poll, resend, Finish connecting state and its card tests) is not in this patch because ConnectorSuggestionCard.tsx is EP-10-S8's new file and is absent from this base, so lead_todo carries the exact calls.

A resumed turn is sent with appendUser false and no client_message_id, the same shape as continue generation, so the live stack must show the gateway does not store the saved question a second time as a user row [verify live].

The Finish connecting state reads the saved record, not the card's own in-flight connect, and runConnectIntent resumes after clearing rather than taking the record, so a Continue click in the same page while a popup is open could send the question twice; the card must show its in-flight state instead.

resumeConnectIntent does not repeat the composer's connector gates (catalogue advertisement, zero retention, Space, filtered sources) and the chat client silently drops connector_scope on subscription-backed turns (chat-client.ts:2122), so the card must offer Connect only where the connected-apps chips are offered.

When the composer is off its default scope or a run is streaming, resumeConnectIntent refuses and the saved connect stays, so the Finish connecting state can persist until the person changes the scope back or the 15 minute TTL passes; the card copy must say so.

No controller-level test covers connectTurn, pendingConnectIntent or resumeConnectIntent and their refusals (other thread, streaming, temporary, Space, foreign origin, non-auto scope) because the controller harness cannot be run in this batch.

The record holds only the question, so a resumed turn runs with the composer's current tools, attachments and source settings rather than the original turn's; the owner should decide whether the record carries the tool choices (design D7 says prompt only).
After a resume the earlier answer that offered the connection stays above the new answer, because appendUser false only appends while regenerate truncates; the owner should choose the reader's view.

An expired record of another thread is removed only when that thread is read again, so the question text can stay in sessionStorage until the tab closes; a sweep of expired keys inside saveIntent would bound it.

The wait polls listConnections, whereas getConnectSessionStatus returns the connection id once the session completes and would identify the new connection exactly; the design names the list, so this is a later option.

deviations: Orchestration (save before the popup, wait for the connection, resend once, Continue after a reload) lives in connect-intent.ts behind injected dependencies rather than in the card, because the card is EP-10-S8's file and is absent from this base; the card keeps the UI and the calls listed in lead_todo.

The connected app for the resumed turn travels as the per-turn connectorScope option of sendContent, not through a chat.set_connector_scope action call: the consent is per turn and no chip state is written, which is what that action contract requires.
resumeConnectIntent refuses on a non-auto retrieval scope or a conversation-only source, the offer rule S8 uses, which the design left implicit.
The Continuing status line uses the page's existing feedback notice (ChatPage.tsx:1471 renders it for six seconds) rather than a new message part.

An earlier attempt had already done most of the work in this worktree. I kept what was right and finished it:
- **Already there (reviewed and kept):**
  - The per-call CONNECT proxy, accepting only `host:443` on a canonical host name. Its DNS guard refuses private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses, and IPv4 addresses mapped into IPv6 or NAT64.
  - The `mp-netbridge` binary (standard library only).
  - `egress_tiers.rs`: closed enum, `min_tier`, strict switch parser, registry list.
  - The bwrap argv: unshares the network, covers the socket root with a tmpfs, binds the call's own socket, and runs the program under the bridge.
  - The executor: admits `AllowDomains` only behind a live per-call proxy in a wrapped process. The `HTTPS_PROXY` check is removed.
  - In `code_interpreter`: the `run_with_egress` seam and the E1 report `network=<tier>, enforcement=full`, plus `egress` counts. The result bytes do not change at off.
  - The capability claim is the switch tier only when bwrap and the bridge are both present; otherwise it stays the legacy word.
  - sandbox-manager: the 0008 migration, `server.go` (D-E2 behind `SANDBOX_MANAGER_EGRESS_TIERS`), and its tests.
- **Added by me:**
  - A per-run registry in `egress_proxy.rs`. `run_egress()` holds `register`, `set_ceiling`, `record_lease` and `call_egress`; a run with no entry is off.
  - `lease_tier`, which maps the proto enum to a tier.
  - `run_ceiling(RunEgressFacts)`: off for ZDR, waived, plan-mode, tainted or read-only-rung runs.
  - In `agent.rs`: the run registers only while the switch is on (guard dropped on any path). Before each `code_interpreter` dispatch, the ceiling is set from the run's current facts. Taint is `read_in_round || ctx.taint.is_marked()`.
  - Tests for all of the above, and an inventory test that pins the ZDR/waived hold.

--unshare-net is unconditional only for calls with an egress bridge (and for Disabled, as before), not for every local run. Making it unconditional would change AllowAll behaviour with the switch off.

What was built:
- New table thread_share_snapshots. It cascades from threads, has the 8 MiB CHECK, and requires that a live row has both a body and a digest while a revoked row has neither. It ships with a revert file.
- New thread_shares.proto with Create, List, Get and Revoke; every field is commented. It is added to build.rs.
- session-core thread_shares.rs:
  - Taking a snapshot reuses the S9 export with the REDACTED profile, so the export's refusals apply (Space thread, any non-persistent run). A ZDR or waived caller is refused first with feature conversation_share.
  - Each thread holds at most 20 live snapshots, enforced under an advisory lock.
  - The insert takes the owner from the thread row and re-checks it.
  - Revoke deletes the body and digest in the same statement.
  - Reads are owner-only. Nothing exists yet that would let session-core check a Control grant for conversation_snapshot, so the risk's fallback applies.
  - The service is registered in grpc.rs, and delete_thread_rows deletes these rows too.
  - The switch is SESSION_THREAD_SHARES_ENABLED. While it is off every RPC answers unavailable thread_shares_disabled.
- model-gateway thread_share_routes.rs:
  - Routes POST/GET /v1/threads/:id/snapshots and GET/DELETE /v1/snapshots/:id.
  - Switch MODEL_GATEWAY_THREAD_SHARES; while it is off every route answers 404 thread_shares_disabled.
  - A ZDR caller is refused at the gateway before taking a snapshot.
  - Errors use the typed envelope with details always an object.
  - A snapshot read is no-store.
  - Unit tests show that an api_key principal is refused on all four routes.
